title.title: Subpolynomial query complexity for log-concave sampling
title.subtitle: Claim: $C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon$ gradient queries suffice to sample a well-conditioned log-concave density

plain: Drawing random samples from a smooth bell-shaped cloud in huge dimension needs almost no gradient queries

object.axisLabel: exponent $e$ in a query bound $d^{e}$, condition number 2

beats.text: Sample from $e^{-V}$ in $d$ dimensions, using value-and-gradient queries of $V$
Standard samplers need a small power of $d$
Claimed: $d^{\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon$, and $\log d$ is necessary

steps: Blur the target with a little random noise
Each blurred piece is an almost bell-shaped problem
Solve those by nesting cheap averages inside each other
Then undo the blur, step by step

voice.text: Sampling a bell curve, nearly free.
Sampling a smooth bell-shaped cloud usually costs a power of the dimension.
Blur the target, solve near-bell pieces by nesting averages, then unblur.
Claimed: d to any epsilon queries suffice.
